input.command: ls -la; cat src/config.ts; grep -rn "ADMIN_CIDR\|auditLog" --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.json . | grep -v node_modules
input.description: List repo, show config, search for usages

input.command: ls -R src; cat package.json; cat -n src/routes.ts; grep -rn "isAdminAddress\|routes\|remoteAddr\|clientIp\|x-forwarded" src

input.description: Search for route wiring and api file

input.reason: I read src/config.ts and src/routes.ts. src/config.ts:3 sets `ADMIN_CIDR = "0.0.0.0/0"`. `isAdminAddress` calls `cidrContains(ADMIN_CIDR, ip)`. In `cidrContains`, `Number(bits) === 0 ? 0 : ...` makes the mask 0, so both sides of the comparison are 0 and the function returns true for every input. Even a malformed or IPv6 address works, because `toInt` returns NaN >>> 0, which is 0, and 0 & 0 is still 0. In src/routes.ts:42-44, `auditLog` has one gate, `if (!isAdminAddress(req.ip)) return { status: 403 }`. It checks no user role or identity, so it always goes on to read AUDIT_LOG and return it. Nothing else in the repository references `auditLog`, `isAdminAddress` or `buildRoutes`, so no other guard exists.
input.summary: ADMIN_CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 makes every client an admin for auditLog

findings.text: The admin allowlist is `0.0.0.0/0`, which spans `0.0.0.0`–`255.255.255.255`, so every client address counts as an admin network and `auditLog` serves the audit log to anyone.
findings.reason: Claim 1, the allowlist is 0.0.0.0/0: src/config.ts:3 reads `export const ADMIN_CIDR = "0.0.0.0/0";`. Claim 2, it spans the whole IPv4 range and every client counts as admin: `cidrContains` sets `mask` to 0 when `Number(bits) === 0`. It then returns `(toInt(base) & 0) === (toInt(ip) & 0)`, which is always true, so `isAdminAddress(ip)` is true for every address. Claim 3, `auditLog` serves the log to anyone: src/routes.ts:43-44 only returns 403 when `!isAdminAddress(req.ip)`. That never happens, so the handler always returns `{ status: 200, body: await readFile(AUDIT_LOG, "utf8") }`. The handler checks no user role, and nothing else in the repository adds a guard.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable authorization bypass. The admin-only `auditLog` endpoint is gated only by `isAdminAddress`, and that check returns true for every address, so any client can read the full audit log file (/var/harbor/audit.log) and no credentials are needed.
